clue.text: Game of a fireside companion?

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players bet on the value of their hands
the iron rod kept beside the hearth for stirring the coals

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a betting card game and the metal rod used to stir a fire, a constant companion of the hearth.

clue.text: Pursue writing-style attractive to Americans

parts.note: prose is the ordinary written style, not verse
cute means attractive in American usage

explanation.surface: A writer chasing a style that will charm American readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a case in law is to bring charges against someone.

clue.text: Jack and King with space in church

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess
the nave is the central area of a church

explanation.surface: Two playing cards laid out in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the jack in a pack of cards, below the queen.

clue.text: Grieves loss of river waders

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
egrets are wading birds of the heron family

explanation.surface: Someone mourning the disappearance of wading birds from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret is to feel sorrow over something lost or missed.

clue.text: Overcoat safe to put on

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to put on an act is to sham, to pretend

explanation.surface: Advice that a coat is a sensible thing to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old thieves' slang, much loved by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham was a heavy overcoat named after the nineteenth-century Viscount Petersham.

clue.text: Dawdle like one, at the wheel?

definitions.meaning: to move about idly without purpose
someone at a turning wheel shaping clay, not a driver

explanation.definitionFit: Means to dawdle about aimlessly and also names a person who throws pots on a wheel.

clue.text: Records attempt in the Gobelin show

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Recordings attempted at a Gobelin exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Gobelin was the famous Paris works for woven wall hangings, so its product is on show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobelin factory in Paris made woven pictorial wall hangings for display.

clue.text: Note goes round showing the polling figures

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
turns means goes round

explanation.surface: A note being passed round showing the voting results.
explanation.walkthrough: Election results are known as the returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Election results reported from each district are officially known by this name.

clue.text: Might this bogey carry one across?

definitions.text: Might this bogey carry one across?

parts.words: Might this bogey carry one across?
parts.note: bogey means a goblin-like spook, and one across is the iron fire tool of 1 across, which a fireside shelf might hold

explanation.walkthrough: 'one across' points to 1 across, the fire iron; a hob is the shelf beside the fire that might carry it, and a goblin is a bogey.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous sprite or bogeyman of folklore.

clue.text: Low quarters of the elk

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
S and E, south and east, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: Lowly parts of an elk's body.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the largest deer is called by this name, while Europeans call it the elk.

clue.text: Operating free-style butterfly

indicators.note: free-style suggests the letters move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A butterfly stroke used in a free-style swimming race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free-style' and 'butterfly' both pretend to be swimming strokes; the first rearranges OPERATING, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European butterfly whose males have orange wing ends.

clue.text: Cricketer returns a pair — which is to be avoided!

indicators.note: returns tells us the cricketer word is read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
in cricket a pair is two ducks, two scores of nothing, shown as two O's

explanation.surface: A batsman getting a pair, two noughts, is something every cricketer dreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns BAT into TAB. A PAIR in cricket means being out for nothing in both innings: O plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom is a thing people must steer clear of.

clue.text: Living in London, he was close to Dickens

definitions.text: Living in London, he was close to Dickens

parts.words: Living in London, he was close to Dickens
parts.note: close means stingy, so this is a London miser created by the novelist, not a friend of his

explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Dickens' reads as a friend of the author; close here means mean with money, and he is Dickens's character.
explanation.definitionFit: The miserly moneylender of A Christmas Carol lived in London and was famously tight-fisted.

clue.text: Article in Le Monde, say, absolutely one-sided

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, as found in a French newspaper
just can mean absolutely, as in just perfect

explanation.surface: A French newspaper report accused of being completely biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfair favours one party, so it is biased or partial.

clue.text: Very high winds in Blackburn, say?

definitions.meaning: fast air currents high in the atmosphere
split as black (jet) and burn (a Scottish word for stream)

explanation.walkthrough: Blackburn is a Lancashire town; split it into BLACK, which is jet, and BURN, the Scottish word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow fast currents of high-altitude air, and black plus burn rendered in synonyms.

clue.text: Patient wife Greek ladies turn out

indicators.note: the ladies and the abbreviation turn out differently, rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-suffering wife watches Greek women turn out for an event.
explanation.walkthrough: GRISELDA is the proverbially patient wife of Chaucer's Clerk's Tale and Boccaccio.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the Clerk's Tale endures her husband's cruel tests without complaint, a byword for marital endurance.

clue.text: Provider of tips for course gives a starting-price with a return of money.

parts.note: SP is the racing abbreviation for starting price

indicators.note: return of means the word for money is read backwards

parts.note: sugar is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A racing tipster at the course gives the starting price and news of winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface hides a vegetable: its tips are eaten at a meal course. 'return of' turns SUGAR into RAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable's edible spear tips are served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Murder-weapon suiting T S Eliot to a T?

indicators.note: suiting suggests the letters are tailored and rearranged

parts.note: a T is the letter T itself

explanation.surface: A murder weapon in a poem that suits the poet perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suiting' rearranges TSELIOT plus the extra T into a dagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender stabbing dagger, used as a weapon for killing.

clue.text: I am in fortune as judge

indicators.note: in means the first words are placed within the word for fortune

parts.note: an estate is a fortune in property
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone declaring that their wealth makes them a good judge.
explanation.walkthrough: I AM becomes IM (I'm, without the apostrophe), placed inside ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to form a judgement of size or value, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: One of the best conductors? (Most are malleable)

indicators.note: malleable means easily shaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A remark that most of the finest conductors are pliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductors' and 'malleable' suggest metals that conduct heat; the definition is a great orchestral conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: A master musician, particularly a distinguished conductor of orchestras.

clue.text: To make car accelerate, begin firing

definitions.meaning: to put your foot down and give the engine full throttle
to start shooting, as guns do

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both letting an engine go full throttle and starting to shoot.

clue.text: Delighted to have rent paid outside

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation for paid goes around the rent word

parts.note: pd is the abbreviation for paid
a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A landlord happy that the rent has come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased means glad or happy, a synonym of delighted.

clue.text: Word of cheer after articulation of two hips?

definitions.text: Word of cheer after articulation of two hips?

parts.words: Word of cheer after articulation of two hips?
parts.note: articulation suggests anatomy, but it means speaking: the cheer that follows shouting hip twice

explanation.walkthrough: 'articulation' and 'hips' suggest joints in anatomy; it is the shout that follows 'hip, hip'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional cheer shouted after a leader calls hip twice.

clue.text: Nude girl, the one at the resort?

definitions.text: Nude girl, the one at the resort?

parts.words: Nude girl, the one at the resort?
parts.note: pictures a young woman at a naturist holiday resort, wearing nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints a naturist resort; the answer is the idiom for being stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wearing no clothes at all, as one would at a naturist camp.

clue.text: Standard way I prepare for 1 ac

parts.note: before a hand of the card game at 1 across, the cards are dealt

explanation.surface: Explaining the usual way of getting ready for a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is the card game at 1 across, which begins with the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard of perfection to aim for is a model or paragon.

clue.text: Derek, they say, is one in the army

definitions.note: Derek sounds like derrick, a crane for lifting loads

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the army word

parts.note: a host is an army
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man named Derek is said to be serving as a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by sound: Derek sounds like derrick, a lifting crane. HOST is an old word for an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a crane, a lifting device.

clue.text: Competition on a par with Towcester's first

parts.note: on a par means level, even

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the racecourse name

explanation.surface: A race meeting at Towcester racecourse, with runners neck and neck.
explanation.walkthrough: Towcester is an English horse-racing course, which fits the sporting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest or race within a sports meeting is one item of the programme.

clue.text: Hiding from farm-work

definitions.meaning: beating grain to separate it from the chaff, an old spelling of threshing

explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating, and also the old farm job of beating out grain.

clue.text: Study of stretches of water on M1? Golly, what a mess!

indicators.note: what a mess suggests the letters are jumbled up

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, giving M and I (1 as the letter I)

explanation.surface: A scientist studying lakes is horrified by the state of traffic on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what a mess!' rearranges ON, MI and GOLLY; the M1 is Britain's chief motorway, with its 1 used as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Limnology is the science of lakes and other inland fresh waters.

clue.text: Makes appointment that shows one's age

definitions.meaning: fixes a time or goes out on romantic engagements
looks old-fashioned, betraying the era it comes from

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers fixing appointments and also betraying when something was made.
